pr_title: Adds Validation for barSize Parameter of RenkoConsolidator Constructor
pr_body:
#### Description
Adds validation for `barSize` parameter of `RenkoConsolidator` constructor since `RenkoConsolidator.BarSize` cannot be negative or zero.

#### Related Issue
Closes #4553 

#### Motivation and Context
Without this validation, available in some constructor overloads, the consolidator throws an unhandled exception `DivideByZeroException`. 

#### How Has This Been Tested?
New unit tests.

issue_context.title: RenkoConsolidator Division By Zero
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
Do not allow setting RenkoConsolidator.BarSize to zero.

#### Actual Behavior
It's possible to set `RenkoConsolidator.BarSize`. It causes unhandled `DivideByZeroException` in `RenkoConsolidator.UpdateClassic`

#### Potential Solution
Thrown `ArgumentException` in `RenkoConsolidator` construction.

#### Reproducing the Problem
```python
renkoConsolidator = RenkoConsolidator(round(self.atr.Current.Value,4))
```
where 
`round(self.atr.Current.Value,4)` is zero.

#### Checklist
- [x] I have completely filled out this template
- [x] I have confirmed that this issue exists on the current `master` branch
- [x] I have confirmed that this is not a duplicate issue by searching [issues](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues)
- [x] I have provided detailed steps to reproduce the issue

review_comments: This API choice concerns me; I think it would be better to split this into a class per Renko or rethink the API for this class so the user can't accidentally cause an explosion by putting a perfectly valid looking arg into the constructor.
This whole class is a candidate for deprecation and replacement with two separate classes; maybe making the old class inherit from its replacement to maintain backward compatibility.
Agree 👍, if `RenkoType` can only have 1 value then it doesn't seem like an argument at all

Cool! 
Could we have the constructors call each other? With these smart constructors, I think it's a nice approach to have them call each other to avoid having to duplicate this logic so many times, which is error-prone too and actually lead to this issue
1e-28 is super small -- I'm guessing an out of range exception brought us here. In my own checks I'll usually limit it to 1e-20 to avoid divisions pushing me out of range.
